Solutions

Dashboards and data systems I've built for Stockton Unified School District, each one aimed at a problem people were actually stuck on. Every figure here is a school- or district-level aggregate cleared for public sharing.

State Assessment Participation Tracker

Power BI · 21-page interactive report

When I took over participation tracking, most of the district was sitting under California's 95% requirement. So I built a live tracker. Every school site can watch its own numbers during testing season, with a gauge for each state assessment (ELPAC, CAASPP, CAA, PFT) and the option to drill down by school and director. Participation went up 3 points, which pushed us over the 95% line.

Districtwide Early Warning System: Harvard Capstone

Harvard Strategic Data Project · Capstone case study

My capstone for the Harvard Strategic Data Project, co-led with Senior Research Analyst Shahed Saif. It's an early warning system covering the district's eleven high schools. The model pulls together attendance, GPA, course performance, behavior, and SAEBRS scores to flag who's on track to graduate and who isn't, then sorts students into support levels and feeds a live dashboard and intervention roster. The whole point is to let counselors and administrators step in before a student falls off track, not after.

CAASPP Preliminary Results Explorer

Power BI · 11-page interactive report

Students took these tests every year, but the results weren't getting back to classrooms in any form teachers could use. So I built this explorer. Teachers and site leaders can see where their students actually stand: achievement levels by grade, average distance from standard, and four-year trends across roughly 19,000 students. It tells them where to put their attention.

ELPAC Summative Results Explorer

Power BI · 4-page interactive report

Same feedback gap, different group: the district's roughly 6,500 English learners. Sites can see how students are doing across listening, speaking, reading, and writing, broken out by school, grade, special education, and 504 status, so they know who still needs language support and where to focus it.
